# Juicescan

> Explorer for Juicebox V6: look up a project, read its rules and balances, and build
> its transactions. A static app on IPFS that reads chain RPCs and the Bendystraw indexer.

## How to read this site as an agent

The app is hash-routed and renders in the browser, so fetching a route returns the
same shell every time. These resources are readable without running JavaScript:

- [Learn Juicebox](./learn.html): the complete Learn guide, generated from the same
  source as the interactive tab. Section fragments such as `#learn-revnets` work.
- [Build with Juicebox](./build.html): the complete Build guide and code examples.
- [Glossary](./learn.html#learn-glossary): short definitions in learning order.
- [Fees](./learn.html#learn-fees): what each fee is, and the tokens fee payers get back.
- [First payment journey](https://juicebox.money/build/first-payment): read a
  testnet project without a wallet, then make and verify a reviewed test payment.
- `/manifest.json`: app identity (also what Safe reads to add this as a Safe App).

Served only by an HTTP host:

- `/?project=<chain>:<projectId>`: the server injects that project's Open Graph title,
  description and card image, and `GET /project-og.png?project=<chain>:<projectId>`
  renders the card as a 1200x630 PNG. Chain slugs: `eth`, `base`, `arb`, `op`, `sep`,
  `basesep`, `arbsep`, `opsep`.

Live project views need the bundle. On an IPFS gateway there is no server, so the
query form above resolves to the generic site card.

## Routes (hash fragments, resolved in the browser)

- `#<chain>:<projectId>`: one project's activity, balance, tokens, holders, shop and rules.
- `#@<handle>`: the same project by its verified ENS handle. The handle is served only
  when ENS and the JBProjectHandles registry agree that the project's current owner or
  operator claimed it.
- `#account/<address-or-ens>`: holdings, roles and activity for one account.
- `#api`: every deployed V6 contract, with ABI, source and read and write forms.
- `#learn`, `#build`, `#why`: the protocol guide, the integration guide, and why Juicebox
  works this way. `#learn-<section>` and `#build-<section>` open a section.
- `#data`: raw indexer queries and CSV exports.
- `#admin`: operator batches.

## Building on this

The Build tab emits ready-to-paste prompts describing each surface's exact contracts,
transaction routes and verification requirements. Prefer those over reverse-engineering
the bundle: they name the same reads and writes this client performs.

## Source

- Protocol contracts: https://github.com/Bananapus/version-6
- This client: https://github.com/mejango/juicescan
- Indexer: https://bendystraw.up.railway.app
